leyline.white:
White leyline mages are the institutional hand on the battlefield — marshals, wardens, and oathkeepers who bend the chaos of a fight into formation. Where they stand, lines hold.

They draw their power from unity rather than self. A White mage rarely wins alone; instead they knit allies into a single coordinated body, steadying the wavering, shielding the exposed, and binding enemies to terms they cannot break.

White Specialties

The White leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Coordination. Marshalling allies into one purpose — guiding signals, shared resolve, and aura healing that keeps a formation moving as a body.

Bulwark. Standing between harm and the vulnerable — interposing shields, retributive guard, and shield walls that turn a line into a wall.

Accord. Authority made binding — terms, oaths, and disciplined will that compel enemies and steel allies against Influence.

Draw Mana: allies within Attunement Range regain Health equal to your Tier.
leyline.blue:
Blue leyline mages read the battle a beat before it happens. Tacticians, augurs, and pattern-readers, they treat combat as a problem already half-solved — every outcome a variable they have learned to weight.

They rarely meet force with force. A Blue mage prefers to know, to prepare, and to redirect: intercepting an attack foreseen, bending probability against an enemy, or raising images and walls that exist only in the mind.

Blue Specialties

The Blue leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Foresight. Knowing the next move — forewarning, interception, telepathic links, and analysis that makes a Reaction the right one.

Calculation. Bending probability — pattern recognition, counterspells, and suggestions that quietly reshape an enemy's choices.

Illusion. Light and lie — phantom walls, holographic doubles, and barriers of pure image that misdirect a foe into the wrong fight.

Draw Mana: gain Advantage on your next Cognitive test.
leyline.black:
Black leyline mages are predators. They thrive where others are alone — cutting a target from the herd, then taking from it in blood, will, and breath until nothing is left to resist.

Their magic exacts a price, and they pay it gladly: Health spent for power, Focus stripped from the enemy mind, Vital wounds that no armor turns aside. Surrounded, a Black mage falters; isolated with their prey, they are inevitable.

Black Specialties

The Black leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Isolation. Punishing the lone and the separated — predatory patience, hexes, and a dread presence that makes solitude lethal.

Ritual. Power bought with blood — sacrificial costs, withering touch, and reservoirs of stolen Investiture.

Subjugation. Seizing the mind — siphoned will, coercive pressure, and commands the depleted cannot refuse.

Draw Mana: enemies within range with no ally within 10 ft become Weakened.
leyline.red:
Red leyline mages burn. Berserkers, firebrands, and stormbringers, they meet violence with greater violence and grow stronger the worse the fight becomes — every wound taken is fuel for the next blow.

They trade defense for devastation. A Red mage drawing power surrenders their guard, throwing everything forward in momentum, flame, and fury. Hesitation is the only thing that cools them.

Red Specialties

The Red leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Momentum. Force that compounds — reckless advances, volatile strikes, and unstoppable charges that hit harder the longer they run.

Conflagration. Pyromancy unleashed — kindling, searing bolts, and chain detonations that turn a battlefield into a furnace.

Frenzy. Passion as a weapon — inciting rage, shattering focus, and a feeding frenzy that escalates past the point of restraint.

Draw Mana: gain Advantage on your next Physical test, but lose your Reaction until your next turn.
leyline.green:
Green leyline mages belong to the wild's logic. Wardens, menders, and pack-leaders, they shape the ground itself and bind their allies into something that hunts and heals as one.

Where Black isolates, Green clusters. A Green mage grows the battlefield against their enemies — thorns and grasping roots, terrain that favors the pack — while knitting deep wounds, even Injuries, that lesser magic cannot touch.

Green Specialties

The Green leyline presents talents in three specialties:

Territory. Owning the ground — grasping vines, thorn fields, and spreading roots that turn the battlefield into a snare.

Restoration. Deep mending — the only leyline healing that closes Injuries, regrowing allies back into the fight.

Instinct. The pack's edge — coordinated hunts, scenting the weak, and warnings that move the whole group as one body.

Draw Mana: create difficult terrain at a point within Attunement Range.

deity.Life:
Anaveth, the Vital Hand, is the deity of Life — growth, healing, and the intimate knowledge of living things. Her blessed are surgeons and shapers who do not merely close wounds but improve the body they mend.

An Anaveth disciple diagnoses before she heals: reading an ally's anatomy to strike an enemy's with precision, then knitting flesh with riders no leyline mender can match — temporary vigor, deflecting hide, mutations that turn a wounded comrade into the battle's engine.

Signature resource: Mutation — a lasting biological boon grafted onto an ally (natural armor, venom, regrowth) that persists for the scene.

Requires attunement to both Blue and Green leylines.
deity.Knowledge:
Gnothis, the Watching Mind, is the deity of Knowledge — but his is the knowledge of the hunt. To study a thing is to learn how to kill it, and to share that study with the pack.

A disciple of Gnothis marks a quarry and accumulates Insight upon it; every observation sharpens the killing blow, and the whole pack profits from what one hunter learns. Patience first, then a strike that lands like a verdict.

Signature resource: Insight — an accumulating mark of study on a quarry; each stack sharpens the damage you and your pack deal to it.

Requires attunement to both Red and Green leylines.
deity.Civilization:
Kethane, the Great Builder, is the deity of Civilization — the forge, the wall, and the bonds that turn a crowd into a community. Her blessed raise works of metal and will that fight on their behalf.

A disciple of Kethane forges a Combat Construct and specializes it for war, repairs and commands it across the field, and binds allies with the shared strength of foundations and trade.

Signature resources: Combat Construct — a persistent forged companion; Foundation — a designated square that steadies allies who hold it.

Requires attunement to both Red and White leylines.
deity.Chaos:
Maelith, the Unmaker of Certainties, is the deity of Chaos — patron of the broken plan and the fatal coincidence. Where order expects a clean result, Maelith inserts a flaw.

A disciple of Maelith forces Complications onto an enemy's actions, then banks that misfortune and spends it: as focus seized, as advantage stolen, as Vital wounds carved into a target left isolated and alone.

Signature resource: Omen — a banked twist of misfortune, gained when you force a Complication onto an enemy and spent to seize focus, steal advantage, or carve Vital damage into an isolated target.

Requires attunement to both Blue and Black leylines.
deity.Death:
Morrath, the Last Harvest, is the deity of Death — not its terror but its husbandry. Her blessed are necromancers who treat the fallen as a crop to be reaped.

A disciple of Morrath kills with withering curses and Death Wards, then harvests the corpse for what remains. Those Harvested Remains fuel her darker work: bone gardens, risen servants, words wrung from the dead, and at the last, the dead made to rise whole.

Signature resource: Harvested Remain — a marker left on a corpse that drops within your range, spent to power Morrath's corpse-magic.

Requires attunement to both Black and Green leylines.
deity.Fate:
Olvarra, the Thread-Reader, is the deity of Fate — the oracle who sets the board before initiative is rolled. Her blessed do not react to the battle; they have already read it.

A disciple of Olvarra anchors allies to Ordained Ground and lays Snares on the squares an enemy has not yet chosen to enter. When the foreseen step comes, the trap is already waiting.

Signature resources: Ordained Ground — an ally-anchored square that fortifies whoever holds it; Snare — a single-use trap sprung by the first enemy to enter.

Requires attunement to both Green and White leylines.
deity.Power:
Tyrith, the Iron Crown, is the deity of Power — domination as an end in itself. His blessed do not persuade; they compel, and they grow with every enemy laid low.

A disciple of Tyrith forces foes to kneel — Compelled, Weakened, made to serve — then exploits the broken and feeds on the kill. Each death builds toward a warlord's fury no single rival can withstand.

Signature resource: Bounty — a tally of the fallen; each enemy slain within your range adds one, escalating your dominating talents toward a warlord's fury.

Requires attunement to both Black and Red leylines.
deity.Destruction:
Razkael, the Sundering Flame, is the deity of Destruction — the siege engineer and pyrotechnician who turns timing into devastation. Nothing he marks survives unbroken.

A disciple of Razkael plants delayed Charges with precision and waits, letting detonations chain across the field and leaving dangerous terrain that keeps burning long after the blast.

Signature resource: Charge — a placed marker with a declared trigger that detonates for area energy damage and scars the ground.

Requires attunement to both Blue and Red leylines.
deity.Order:
Tessavain, the Lawgiver, is the deity of Order — patron of oath, pact, and prohibition. His word, once given, binds both ways.

A disciple of Tessavain declares Edicts that punish the first forbidden act and swears Covenants that fortify sworn allies. To break his law is to be struck by it; to keep it is to be shielded.

Signature resources: Edict — a prohibition that punishes the forbidden action; Covenant — a sworn pact that fortifies both partners.

Requires attunement to both Blue and White leylines.
deity.Sovereignty:
Verdannis, the Crowned Arbiter, is the deity of Sovereignty — the right to raise and to cast down. His blessed rule the battlefield as a court, elevating one and diminishing another with the same gesture.

A disciple of Verdannis diminishes an enemy with one hand and exalts an ally with the other, drawing both into Decrees — declared laws that hold sway within his reach.

Signature resource: Decree — a declared law projected within a radius: allies inside are elevated, enemies inside are diminished.

Requires attunement to both Black and White leylines.

heroic.Hunter:
The thrill of the chase thrums in a Hunter’s mind as they patiently surveil. No detail is too small or insignificant to ignore. Experience teaches the most important lesson: you don’t have to be more powerful than your quarry, so long as you’re better prepared.

Through careful planning, Hunters choose when and where to strike, securing an upper hand through clever use of traps, high ground, and the element of surprise. If all goes well, the quarry won’t perceive their assailant until it’s too late. Some Hunters prefer a clean kill from afar. Others make their work personal, striking in close quarters and taking pleasure in their prey’s visceral panic; nothing feels sweeter than methodical preparation culminating in an exhilarating onslaught.

Hunter Specialties

The Hunter path presents talents in three specialties:

Archer. Targeting weak points in an enemy army’s assault, Archers shape the battlefield before the frontline confrontation. They steadily unleash a torrent of arrows to scatter and terrorize foes.

Assassin. Whether commissioned to kill or driven by their own interests, Assassins exploit weaknesses to quickly incapacitate their quarry.

Tracker. In untamed wilds, none are more capable than Trackers. With trusty animal companions at their sides, they scrounge provisions, deftly cross unfriendly terrain, and set perilous traps. Available in the Stormlight Handbook.

Building a Hunter

Consider these general tips for building an effective Hunter:

Attributes. It’s usually a good idea to prioritize Awareness, Strength, and Speed.

Skills. Useful skills include Agility, Perception, Stealth, Survival, and either Light Weaponry or Heavy Weaponry.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.kWWyJQRYlIMoQCe9]{Warrior} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.qqa1ZgA957Cae6ex]{Agent} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can’t go wrong with an animal companion, a grandbow, or a Shardblade.

Hunter Key Talent

The Hunter key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.3nfGn0BOeLq5qgEr]{Seek Quarry}, unlocks access to the Hunter specialties.

Starting Skill: Perception. If you choose Hunter as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Perception.
heroic.Envoy:
Prominent organizations throughout Roshar appoint Envoys who vie for resources, curry favor, or offer service on the organization’s behalf. These stewards dutifully further the reach of their ideologies through precise rhetoric, patient attendance, and ceaseless fervor.

Envoys typically subscribe to well-established beliefs and are careful not to disrupt the integrity of those tenets with personal desires and ambitions. Wherever they go, an Envoy stays rooted in their ethos through their strong connection to the entity they serve. Though an Envoy considers themself part of something much grander, their personality shapes the way they fulfill their duties—and thus they shape the organization they serve.

Envoy Specialties

The Envoy path presents talents in three specialties:

Diplomat. Stationed abroad, Diplomats are adept at navigating court politics. They use what they learn about their host countries to seek more favorable treatment for their own.

Faithful. For Faithful, worship of the divine permeates their entire lives. They devote themselves to the traditions of their faith, demonstrating their convictions to others through word or deed.

Mentor. More interested in the individual than the whole, Mentors devote themselves to their wards. They patiently nurture others toward greatness, seeing beyond doubts and deficits to stoke each person’s potential. Available in the Stormlight Handbook.

Building an Envoy

Consider these general tips for building an effective Envoy:

Attributes. It’s usually a good idea to prioritize Presence and Willpower.

Skills. Discipline is an essential skill for most Envoys. Other useful skills include Deception, Leadership, Lore, and Persuasion.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.spF8y5TmLUxxMfxm]{Leader} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.oFA1jJZQMhTUjyem]{Scholar} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can’t go wrong with influential patrons.

Envoy Key Talent

The Envoy key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.l4wRQT2MH0SsxmRQ]{Rousing Presence}, unlocks access to the Envoy specialties.

Starting Skill: Discipline. If you choose Envoy as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Discipline.
heroic.Warrior:
Roshar is a world riven by conflict, and many of its people follow the path of the Warrior, whether for good or ill. A Warrior might view fighting as a calling, an ethos, a profession, or simply an unpleasant necessity for survival—but in all cases, battle follows the Warrior like a shadow.

Those who survive long enough to become seasoned fighters tend to be tough, resilient, and skilled at inflicting harm. An experienced Warrior can handle themself in any dangerous martial situation, whether a formal duel, an alleyway scuffle, or a terrifying clash of armies.

Warrior Specialties

The Warrior path presents talents in three specialties:

Duelist. In the inner circles of the elite, skilled Duelists contend for glory and political sway, wielding their weapons with brutal grace.

Shardbearer. Warriors fortunate enough to own (or borrow) Shardblades and Shardplate serve as Shardbearers. They wield these arms and armor of ancient provenance to dominate the battlefield with mythic might. Available in the Stormlight Handbook.

Soldier. The most common of fighting forces, Soldiers form the bulk of Roshar’s massive armies. They master the tactics needed to fight effectively in units and stay alive in a deadly world.

Building a Warrior

Consider these general tips for building an effective Warrior:

Attributes. It’s usually a good idea to prioritize Speed and Strength, then consider Awareness and Willpower.

Skills. Useful skills include Athletics, Light Weaponry, Heavy Weaponry, Intimidation, Leadership, and Persuasion.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.spF8y5TmLUxxMfxm]{Leader} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.E6O5QgdG1JxA7tnf]{Hunter} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can’t go wrong with a Shardblade, Shardplate, and a fancy military title.

Warrior Key Talent

The Warrior key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.8mJC2HnsN3OQ2J20]{Vigilant Stance}, unlocks access to the Warrior specialties.

Starting Skill: Athletics. If you choose Warrior as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Athletics.
heroic.Scholar:
Creativity, acumen, and patience are hallmarks of legendary Scholars. Each time a Desolation sweeps away centuries of progress and scientific advancement, Scholars rise to build Roshar anew.

To a Scholar, every mystery is a challenge with a befitting prize. Some Scholars devote their research to famines, barren lands, and related food crises. Others study the body, how it functions, and how to restore it after injury and illness. But not all Scholars occupy themselves with bettering society—some instead pursue tools of destruction. Military Scholars often devise new instruments of war and calculate how to best pressure enemy forces.

No matter their field of study, Scholars use their insatiable hunger for knowledge to change the world for better or worse, one brilliant discovery at a time.

Scholar Specialties

The Scholar path presents talents in three specialties:

Artifabrian. Combining science, engineering, and artistry, Artifabrians use polestones and metal casings to construct fabrials that perform precise functions. Available in the Stormlight Handbook.

Strategist. Always three steps ahead, Strategists know timing is everything and make it work to their benefit.

Surgeon. Qualified Surgeons apply their knowledge and empathy to heal the unwell and save lives.

Building a Scholar

Consider these general tips for building an effective Scholar:

Attributes. It’s usually a good idea to prioritize Intellect above all else, then Presence plus either Speed or Strength (depending on your desired combat functionality).

Skills. Useful skills include Crafting, Deduction, Lore, and Medicine.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.qqa1ZgA957Cae6ex]{Agent} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.axOgzq972lY7la00]{Envoy} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can’t go wrong with fabrials, a companion to mentor, and a Soulcaster.

Scholar Key Talent

The Scholar key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.8FYBJZC8PBjneOim]{Erudition}, unlocks access to the Scholar specialties.

Starting Skill: Lore. If you choose Scholar as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Lore.
heroic.Agent:
Artists of duplicity and sabotage, Agents grasp the threads of fate in the palms of their hands, waiting for the perfect moment to pull and unravel the carefully laid plans of others. Agents can fool even the most prudent with their clever ruses, swift movements, and calculated strikes.

Formal education matters little to Agents. Most are fiercely observant and either self-taught or trained in action by their crew. Rules and regulations from outside entities are but playthings to work around or disregard altogether, and Agents answer only to their own code. They meet impossible tasks with a sly smile and razor-sharp wit, living for the thrill of cheating death yet again.

Agent Specialties

The Agent path presents talents in three specialties:

Investigator. Hunches tend to be unreliable—but Investigators cultivate trustworthy instincts, learning to listen, collaborate, and pursue answers to questions others don’t think to ask. Available in the Stormlight Handbook.

Spy. To get what they need, Spies plant themselves in sticky situations, ready to deflect or ease suspicion when it inevitably sweeps their way.

Thief. Although a quick mind is an invaluable asset, Thieves train their bodies to keep pace. Whether out of necessity or ambition, they risk it all to swindle the insurmountable odds standing between them and their prize.

Building an Agent

Consider these general tips for building an effective Agent:

Attributes. It’s usually a good idea to prioritize Awareness, Intellect, and Speed.

Skills. Useful skills include Agility, Deception, Deduction, Insight, Light Weaponry, and Thievery.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.E6O5QgdG1JxA7tnf]{Hunter} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.oFA1jJZQMhTUjyem]{Scholar} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can’t go wrong with a bodyguard companion and patrons from the criminal world or high society.

Agent Key Talent

The Agent key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.ScqSKbkewDAfSizP]{Opportunist}, unlocks access to the Agent specialties.

Starting Skill: Insight. If you choose Agent as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Insight.
heroic.Leader:
Beacons of encouragement and direction, leaders oversee the efforts of others. Some are born with an unquenchable thirst for power and influence. Others solemnly accept their calling out of a sense of duty. Either way, skilled leadership requires both natural aptitude and dedicated learning. Mistakes are unavoidable, and indecision is a costly pitfall.

When worsening conditions cause followers to doubt, Leaders rise to the occasion, bolstering fellowship and resolve to carry on. Though filling this role often proves lonely and burdensome, Leaders can gloriously turn the tides of fate and prevail against superior forces.

Leader Specialties

The Leader path presents talents in three specialties:

Champion. Inspiring others through unfaltering grit, Champions ferociously charge their foes. Their momentum is magnetic, rallying nearby allies to press on.

Officer. Officers coolly maintain order in utter chaos. They allocate resources and issue commands, orchestrating the march to victory.

Politico. With a penchant for theatrics, Politicos chase favor and prestige while subtly undermining their enemies. Available in the Stormlight Handbook.

Building a Leader

Consider these general tips for building an effective Leader:

Attributes. It’s usually a good idea to prioritize Presence, Strength, and Willpower.

Skills. Useful skills include Athletics, Deception, Heavy Weaponry, Intimidation, Leadership, and Persuasion.

Other Heroic Paths. The @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.kWWyJQRYlIMoQCe9]{Warrior} and @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.axOgzq972lY7la00]{Envoy} paths make excellent multi-path choices.

Rewards. When choosing rewards, you can’t go wrong with a mount companion, high-ranking military title, and possibly even Shardplate.

Leader Key Talent

The Leader key talent, @UUID[Compendium.cosmere-rpg.heroic-paths.Item.UEaOm4P2UFcrP1Z8]{Decisive Command}, unlocks access to the Leader specialties.

Starting Skill: Leadership. If you choose Leader as your starting path, gain a free skill rank in Leadership.
